item.title: Heidi Levine undergoes surgery on 'nearly detached' finger, daughter says
item.description:
Heidi Levine undergoes surgery on 'nearly detached' finger, daughter says

Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, who was brutally attacked by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank, has undergone surgery on her finger, which was nearly detached from her hand during the attack, her daughter has said.

Ashley Milner told The Associated Press that Levine also has a broken rib and multiple broken vertebrae as well as lacerations.

Speaking from her hospital bed on Friday, Levine recounted how the settlers kept kicking her after knocking her down and recalled how her son would often tell her that his biggest fear has been that his mother "would be killed by settlers".

“I was attacked, pushed to the ground. Luckily I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn’t even be here, because they just kept kicking me and kicking me.”

Israeli military sat on distress calls about settler attacks for two hours, report says
item.description:
Israeli military sat on distress calls about settler attacks for two hours, report says

The Israeli military sat on distress calls for nearly two hours as activists reported threats from settlers in the occupied West Bank, but took no action until the attack on diplomats and others was over, the Haaretz daily reports.

The report said that Israeli military operations room received reports about the threats and calls for help as early as 1 pm on Saturday. Yet the Civil Administration and troops on the ground were informed of the attack only around 3 pm, after the attacks had ended.

One activist accompanying local Palestinians reportedly sent the army a video and the exact location of the incident, warning: “At least seven masked settlers armed with clubs. Come quickly, very scary. They stole bags of olives from Palestinians.”

The military has opened a special probe into the sequence of events and why no action was taken in real time to prevent the violence, Haaretz reports.

Israeli rights group, Yesh Din, has said that it documented 377 incidents of settler and soldier violence against Palestinians from 27 September  to 10 October, adding an average of approximately 27 incidents of violence occurred per day across 162 Palestinian communities in the West Bank.

Of these incidents, 174 were directly related to the olive harvest, and soldiers were present in 25 percent of the cases.

"The lack of law enforcement against violent settlers and soldiers who attack Palestinian olive harvesters, damage olive trees, and steal the harvest indicates that the obstruction of the olive harvest is part of a broader, systematic Israeli policy aimed at inflicting economic and cultural harm on Palestinians and displacing them from their land," Yesh Din said in a statement on X.

item.title: Araghchi says Iran has presented 'concrete' Hormuz reopening proposal
item.description:
Araghchi says Iran has presented 'concrete' Hormuz reopening proposal

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran has presented a concrete seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Press TV reported.

Speaking at the 52nd Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) in Baghdad on Saturday, Araghchi said Tehran had conveyed the proposal through Qatar and is prepared to restore passage through the strategic waterway if the necessary conditions were met, the report said.

At the same time, Araghchi said that the United States cannot expect maritime security to return to normal while continuing to exert military pressure on Iran, blaming US and Israeli war on the country for disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.

“Security cannot be restored by more of the same,” he said. “One cannot bomb a country, threaten its annihilation and impose a blockade, and then expect the security of navigation to return to normal.”

Araghchi said Iran and the United States signed a memorandum of understanding in Islamabad on June 17 and subsequently begun technical discussions with Oman to facilitate the safe passage of vessels.

But Tehran's repeated attempts to pursue negotiations in good faith were met with military action, he said, creating deep distrust in the prospects for renewed talks without credible guarantees against a recurrence.

Despite those concerns, he said, Iran had kept the door to diplomacy open.

item.title: Belgium condemns attack by Israeli occupiers on Palestinians, diplomats in West Bank
item.description: Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot on Saturday strongly condemned an attack by masked Israeli occupiers against Palestinians, diplomats and Catholic representatives in Taybeh in the occupied West Bank, Anadolu reports. “I condemn in the strongest terms the attack by masked settlers in Taybeh, in the occupied West Bank, against Palestinians, our Consul General, French and Polish diplomats as well as catholic representatives. A French mayor was assaulted and a Belgian vehicle damaged. Our team is safe,” Prevot said. He stressed that Palestinians face such violence daily, with occupiers also targeting journalists and diplomats. “Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack,” he said on US social media company X. US Rep. Ilhan Omar challenges legality of FBI home search: WSJ
item.description: The defense of US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar have challenged the legality of a search of her Washington home, demanding that federal prosecutors immediately return all seized property and provide recordings made during the operation, The Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday. In a letter sent late Friday, the Minnesota Democrat’s legal team argued that the search, conducted by Homeland Security Investigations agents early Monday under a federal judge-approved warrant, was “neither justified nor lawful.” According to the Journal, the investigation focuses partly on how Omar, 44, obtained US citizenship after arriving from Somalia decades ago. “There is no legitimate basis for any suggestion that she has violated any law concerning her citizenship status,” the letter said. item.title: Israeli occupiers attack European diplomatic delegation in occupied West Bank
item.description: Israeli occupiers attacked a diplomatic delegation comprising representatives from France, Belgium and Poland on Saturday while visiting the town of Taybeh, central occupied West Bank, causing injuries. The attack took place after an official ceremony marking the signing of a twinning agreement between the Palestinian town of Taybeh and the French town of Saint-Pierre, Taybeh Mayor Suleiman Khourieh told Anadolu Agency. The ceremony was attended by the French and Belgian consuls, a Polish representative whose name was not disclosed, and Saint-Pierre Mayor Christian Ravain. The attack targeted the delegation in the western part of the town, as well as Palestinians who were picking olives.
